chapter: Ellington, singers, the book and closing
title: Why jazz dates rarely used singers: Sarah Vaughan and Billie Holiday
summary: Singers who live the lyrics are hard to find; Billie shocked him with her cursing.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Another thing I was thinking on the way up, except for very few times, I don't remember your using
many singers on dates.
Singers?
Yeah.
They're very hard to find.
Why are they hard to find?
Because they ain't singing.
Yeah, all right, what do you look for?
Sarah Vaughan.
Yeah.

Billie Holiday, really, somebody who lives the lyrics. And not really do that much singing, because Billie Holiday -- Sarah Vaughan's a singer. Billie Holiday wasn't a singer. She was a toolsmith. She talked the lyrics a lot.
Yeah, especially in the last few years.
Yeah, she lives them.
Yeah. Did you ever have much conversation with Billie?
A little bit. It's in the book, what I had with her.
Yeah.
I was aloof of her and Duke, very much.
In later years I got to know Duke better but I never got to know Billie. Billie shocked me with her language. I used to never curse in those days.
Really?
Yeah, I never heard anybody curse the way she cursed.
Boy, she could really go on.
Yeah. You could hear her from a distance (inaudible) her dressing room.
Yeah.
I couldn't believe in that.
